title: kith-core: ResultReference and Argument types
description:
What: Define ResultReference and Argument<T> types in src/resultref.rs.

Module file: crates/kith-core/src/resultref.rs — create this file, then add 'pub mod resultref;' to src/lib.rs.

Algorithm:
1. Define ResultReference struct:
   result_of: String  → #[serde(rename="resultOf")]  (call-id of prior invocation)
   name: String  (method name of prior invocation, e.g. "Contact/get")
   path: String  (JSON Pointer per RFC 6901, e.g. "/list/0/id")
   Derives: Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize.
2. Define Argument<T> enum for JMAP argument fields:
   pub enum Argument<T> {
     Value(T),
     Ref(ResultReference),
   }
   Derives: Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize with #[serde(untagged)].
   The untagged repr means: try to deserialize as T first; if that fails, try ResultReference.
   For serialization, both variants serialize transparently.
3. Add 'pub mod resultref;' to src/lib.rs.
4. Run: cargo check -p kith-core

Defensive programming rules:
- Argument<T> uses #[serde(untagged)] — this means deserialization tries T first, then Ref
  Order matters: if T is also a struct with similar fields, ambiguity arises. Document this.
- path field is a JSON Pointer string — the kith-jmap resolver validates it, not kith-core
- No validation in these types

Tests (independent oracle: RFC 8620 §9 ResultReference example):
- ResultReference round-trip: construct {resultOf:"0", name:"Contact/get", path:"/list/0/id"}, serialize, deserialize, assert equality
- Argument::Value(42u32): serializes as just 42 (not wrapped)
- Argument::Ref(rr): serializes as the ResultReference object
- Argument<Vec<String>> deserialization: JSON array ["a","b"] → Argument::Value(["a","b"])
